DEFECT 26, reflow does break it and not where you looked. The CLASSIFIED keys are reflow-safe: they are rebuilt from the match groups as value plus one space, so a wrapped '26 commits' still keys as '26 commits'. Rewrapping the sections' prose at 55 and at 72 columns passes. What breaks are the two scrubbers, the ISO-date one and the decision-filename one, which are the only regexes in this module that are not whitespace-tolerant - both use a literal hyphen class and require the whole token to be contiguous. Minimal realistic trigger: one decision reference wrapped across a line, which is ordinary editing at this repository's column convention. The test then fails naming ['0050-verification-budget-'], a fragment of a filename, as an unclassified count on a page that carries no such count. Every claim pattern learned to accept any whitespace in round one; the scrubbers did not

DEFECT 27, the allowlist matches by value and noun with no position, so a new pair silently inherits an old ruling. Planted 'The queue holds 8 reports awaiting review.' into the Repository snapshot section: the classification test PASSES, because '8 reports' is already classified as day-two historical. The docstring's promise - the key is the matched text, so a changed figure comes back for a fresh ruling - holds for a figure that changes and not for a second occurrence of one that did not
